title: Install the ProxyPilot certificate
subtitle: Lets ProxyPilot decrypt HTTPS traffic from this device. Only do this on a device you use for testing.
checkProxy: Device sends traffic through the proxy
checkProxyTodo: Set this device's Wi-Fi proxy to {addr} (steps below)
checkTrustRejected: {host} rejected the certificate: trust it, then retry
proxyFirst: First set the Wi-Fi proxy: Settings → Wi-Fi → (i) next to your network → Configure Proxy → Manual → Server {host}, Port {port}. Then open http://proxypilot.cert.
iosSteps: Tap Download profile and choose Allow.
Open Settings → Profile Downloaded → Install, then enter your passcode.
Go to Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.
Turn on full trust for “{cn}”. This page updates when HTTPS works.
androidSteps: Set the Wi-Fi proxy: Settings → Network → Wi-Fi → your network → Edit → Advanced → Proxy: Manual, host {host}, port {port}.
Open Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate, and pick proxypilot-ca.crt.
Apps only trust user CAs in debug builds (network_security_config). Browsers work right away.
otherSteps: Download the certificate and add it to the system or browser trust store as a root CA.
Point the device's HTTP and HTTPS proxy at {host}:{port}.
footer: Fingerprint SHA-256 {fp}. Remove it from Settings when you finish testing.
done: All set. Requests from this device appear in ProxyPilot.
